newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian unions plan action to promote jobs pact.
newsitem.headline: Italian unions plan action to promote jobs pact.

text.p: Italy's trade unions said on Friday it planned a series of initiatives, culminating in strike action, to put pressure on the government to speed the passage of a decree law aimed at boosting jobs.
The leaders of the three main union confederations said the industrial action would kick off on May 28 with two-hour shop floor meeting across Italy to discuss the work issue.
"We've decided to dedicate May 28 to workers..and to hold two-hour meetings in all work places," Sergio Cofferati, head of the CGIL confederation -- Italy's largest union body.
Unions said strikes would then proceed on a region by region basis, with emphasis given to poor southern areas. A general strike has already been called for the island of Sardinia on June 10.
"The goal is to keep the pressure on the issue of work because we feel that delays in the passage of the 'jobs pact' have been inexcusable," said Sergio D'Antoni, head of the CISL confederation.

Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Friday the government might call a confidence vote to speed up passage of the so-called 'jobs pact', a decree law which aims to simplify procedures to free up public expenditure on jobs.
He said the bill would be sent to parliament next week and the centre-left government would decide whether to call a confidence test to sweep aside blocking amendments.
The package, approved by the cabinet last month, is designed to complete provisions made in a September pact between government, unions and employers to boost jobs.

Cofferati also urged the government to open talks on welfare reform with union leaders before it presents its latest three year rolling economic programme (DPEF), which is due to be unveiled by the end of the month.

The government has said the document will indicate expected savings from an eventual reform of social spending. Cofferati said that in his eyes, welfare reform did not mean cutbacks but a redistribution of the spending. -- Rome newsroom +396 678 2501
